about_company.about_short: Builds high-reliability electronics for defence, aerospace, industrial and medical customers.
about_company.business_intro: Vinyas is an electronics manufacturing services provider for mission-critical, high-mix programmes. It earns revenue by assembling printed circuit boards, integrating systems and subsystems, building cable harnesses and supporting products through their lifecycle for OEMs, Tier-1 suppliers and defence customers.
about_company.about_long: Vinyas manufactures electronics for defence and aerospace, industrial, medical and transportation applications. Its work spans build-to-print PCB assembly, electro-mechanical integration, cable harnesses, functional testing and lifecycle support. Defence and aerospace are the largest end-markets, while management is adding system-integration work and qualifying for commercial aerospace, medical and export-controlled programmes.

business_facts.text: Vinyas provides PCB assembly, system-level manufacturing, subsystem integration and lifecycle support. It works on long-cycle, high-reliability programmes for global OEMs, Tier-1 suppliers and Indian defence customers rather than mass-market consumer electronics. By end-market, defence and aerospace contributed 78.5% of H1 FY26 operating revenue, industrial electronics 18.5%, medical 1.3% and other businesses 1.7%.
business_facts.title: How it earns
Defence PSUs are the top customers among 100+
business_facts.text: The FY26 annual report counts 100+ customers. Management said the top customers are the defence public sector undertakings, followed by private Indian defence companies. In FY26 Vinyas added 4 defence and aerospace, 3 industrial and 1 medical-device customer logos. The company does not disclose what share of revenue its largest customers make up.

business_facts.title: Exports were about half of FY26 revenue
business_facts.text: Management said exports were almost 50% of FY26 revenue, coming from Europe and the US together, with Europe a little larger than the US. It expects the domestic-to-export split to stay around 50:50. The annual report does not split revenue by geography.

business_facts.title: Order book
business_facts.text: The order book was ₹1,309.06 crore at 31 March 2026, after ₹960.38 crore of order inflow in FY26. The investor presentation splits it into ₹793 crore for the defence and aerospace programme pipeline, ₹324 crore for system integration, ₹112 crore for licence- and certification-led work, ₹45 crore for technology transfer and ₹35 crore for the medical and commercial-aerospace verticals. Management said defence makes up almost 85% to 90% of the order book; other segments run on rolling forecasts.

business_facts.title: Manufacturing base
business_facts.text: Vinyas operates one 1,50,000 sq ft manufacturing unit in Mysuru for printed-board assembly, cable harnesses, electro-mechanical work, functional testing and system integration. The FY26 annual report counts 413 employees; the FY26 investor presentation says 500+ team members, and the two figures are not reconciled. Work began in FY26 on an additional 25,000 sq ft Class 3 facility for system integration; it is not yet operating and no completion date is given (capital work in progress was ₹4.50 crore at 31 March 2026). Management expects utilisation of about 35% to 40% once the added capacity is in place.

Certifications disclosed include NADCAP AC7120 for electronics printed-board assemblies (achieved June 2025), AS9100-D for aerospace, IATF 16949 for automotive and ISO 13485 for medical devices, and Vinyas holds a Government of India defence industry licence. NADCAP enables qualification for programmes that require that accreditation; it does not itself represent an order.
business_facts.title: Quality credentials
Warrant issue for scale-up
business_facts.text: On 3 September 2025 Vinyas allotted 13,64,000 convertible warrants at ₹1,100 each to promoter and non-promoter investors, an issue size of ₹150.04 crore. Each warrant converts into one equity share within 18 months of allotment once the balance is paid. By 31 March 2026 the company had received ₹61.25 crore and used ₹53.25 crore of it for working capital, capital expenditure and general corporate purposes.

business_facts.title: New associates, an Israeli JV and two subsidiaries
business_facts.text: Vinyas holds 26% of Nexus Advanced Technologies, set up for defence manufacturing, and 49% of United Vinyas Technologies Inc., aimed at US defence and aerospace electronics; both associates are expected to buy from Vinyas. Shareholders are asked to approve related-party transactions of up to ₹400 crore with Nexus and ₹150 crore with United Vinyas; these are limits, not revenue. Vinyas also signed a joint venture agreement with an Israeli defence company to make defence systems in India, and set up two wholly owned subsidiaries in FY26, in India and the US. FY26 consolidated revenue equals standalone.

what_changed.text: Industrial electronics rose from 10.7% of FY24 operating revenue to 18.4% in FY25 and 18.5% in H1 FY26. Vinyas also says it has moved from PCB assembly into qualified system integration, commissioned a medical-device line and entered the commercial-aerospace supply chain; these newer verticals remain much smaller than defence and aerospace.
what_changed.headline: The mix is broadening beyond defence assembly.
